newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes soft on dlr cover, Cetes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes soft on dlr cover, Cetes.

text.p: The Mexican peso reversed early gains to close weaker against the dollar on Tuesday due to local dealers taking advantage of a relatively cheaper dollar to cover short positions and expectations of a fall in interest rates, traders said.

"The market was mixed throughout the day," said a trader. "We saw dollars flow in from foreign investors stepping in to the Mexican markets, then the peso slipped again as dealers covered short dollar positions at relatively low prices (in pesos)."
The benchmark 48-hour and 24-hour peso contracts closed 1.95 and two centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.9125/7.9175 and 7.9050/7.9150 per dollar.
The same-day peso had closed earlier 2.7 centavos firmer at 7.8800/7.8900 per dollar.
Traders also put late softness in the peso down to a forecasted fall in primary Cetes rates at Tuesday evening's central bank auction.
A Reuters survey of ten money market traders showed an average expectation that the bellwether 28-day Cete would be assigned at 29.13 percent, or 21 basis points below last week's rate.
"I feel the market had already largely discounted a fall in Cetes, but I think it still may have prompted some dealers to take dollar positions again," said a trader.
Other traders said that dollars may have been bought by dealers hedging against the outcome of U.S. elections on Tuesday and local elections in Mexico on Sunday.
Traders said that the peso's performance on Wednesday would depend to a large extent on the outcome of the Cetes auction.
